narrative:
The model predicts you have a 78% chance of leaving your job, which is why your promotion request was denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart soon, based on patterns from many similar employees.

Three factors stood out most in this decision. First, your 11 or more years of total professional experience was the strongest influence pushing the prediction toward leaving. While only 14.7% of employees predicted to stay have this much experience, the model has learned that people with such long careers often explore new opportunities elsewhere. Second, the fact that you have not received other job offers while at this company worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward staying. Most employees the model expects to remain (76.7%) also report no external offers, so this absence of alternatives slightly reduced the likelihood of departure. Third, having spent only 1-5 years in your current role was another notable push toward leaving. This shorter tenure here, compared to your overall career length, signals to the model that you may still be evaluating whether this organization is the right long-term fit.

The company should discuss your career goals with you openly and explore ways to increase your sense of stability and recognition. You may want to reflect on what would make you want to stay and grow here. Addressing these points could change the outlook for future opportunities. (248 words)
